summary.headline: Ahluwalia Q1 FY27 PAT fell 77.65% to INR11.42 crore on 4.29% EBITDA margin, as AIIMS Jammu bill cut and NCR labour cost spike hit margins; FY27 double-digit margin ruled out.
summary.overview: Turnover rose 12.03% YoY to INR1,125.81 crore, but PAT fell to INR11.42 crore from INR51.11 crore, with EBITDA margin at 4.29% versus 8.59%. Management attributed the drop to a INR29 crore AIIMS Jammu bill reduction (2.6 percentage points), labour cost increases of roughly 35-40% in NCR (about 50% of the order book), higher staff costs, and SIR/election-related disruption in West Bengal and Assam. Net order book stands at INR20,663.52 crore, with only INR512.81 crore of inflow in FY27 to date. Management guided to 12-15% top-line growth but ruled out double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, and did not give a firm date for margin recovery.

financial_highlights.value: Sharp increase YoY; mgmt expects similar ~INR15-16 crore per quarter
financial_highlights.change: due to mobilisation advance for Central Vista

segments.name: NCR projects (about 50% of order book)
segments.commentary: Labour minimum wages rose about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled categories in Haryana and UP, with projects running at 40-50% labour strength. Management estimated a company-level EBITDA hit of about 1.5% this quarter, up to 5% of turnover on some projects where material is client-issued.

segments.name: AIIMS Jammu
segments.commentary: Final bill reduced by INR29 crore after finalisation; the matter is going to arbitration. Impact is 2.6 percentage points on EBITDA. Management says the project is closed and no further hit is expected.

segments.name: Central Vista (Ministry of Housing/CPWD-type govt project)
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR700 crore billing in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore in FY28, with Nirman Bhawan demolition complete and Udyog Bhawan 90% demolished. Full project completes in FY29.

segments.name: CST (Mumbai railway station project)
segments.commentary: Q1 billing about INR70 crore; management targets about INR400-450 crore for FY27 (hoping to cross INR500 crore total) and about INR700 crore in FY28. Earlier target was about INR600 crore.

segments.name: Gems and Jewellery Park
segments.commentary: Work on ground delayed by client design changes; expected to start in Q3 FY27. Targets INR100 crore billing in FY27 and about INR450 crore in FY28; 3.5-year completion.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guidance of 12-15% for FY27 retained, with the low end attributed to NGT uncertainty.
No double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27; management hopes to return to Q1 FY26-level margins over the next three quarters, but gave no firm timeline.
Expects some client compensation for labour cost increases to flow over the next two quarters; NGT impact on Q3 unquantified.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR4,000-5,000 crore versus earlier INR8,000 crore guidance; bidding to be less aggressive.
FY27 capex cut to INR220-250 crore (from about INR300 crore); Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Working capital expected to improve from current level (119 days), with Assam receivables collection resuming.
Expects double-digit margin aspiration for FY28 but said it is hard to predict.
capex_capacity: Capex guided at INR220-250 crore for FY27, down from about INR300 crore earlier; Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Depreciation is elevated and expected to recur given higher capex over the last 2-3 years.
Machinery investment planned to offset labour shortages, and digitisation is in progress.

Central Vista: Nirman Bhawan fully demolished, foundation casting begun, structural steel work from September; Udyog Bhawan handed over about 3 weeks ago with excavation started. About 50% of the job to be commissioned by end of next year.
Dahlias (DLF) and DLF Downtown (about INR1,600-1,700 crore) projects delayed by design changes; billing targets INR30-35 crore/month from Dahlias and INR25-30 crore/month from DLF Downtown.
demand_pricing: Net order book INR20,663.52 crore; private sector about 62% of order book; fixed-price contracts about 10.34%.

Order inflow only INR512.81 crore in FY27 to date; RML (about INR500 crore) is L1 but not converted. Odisha government university bid (about INR1,620 crore L1 hospital/university) lapsed after the company refused a bid validity extension on a fixed-price contract.

Management is deliberately less aggressive in bidding given material and labour volatility; bid prices now factor in labour, doubled shuttering and steel rates, and staff costs above 5% (up from 3.5-4.5%).

Materials: cement and steel are pass-through (about 30-day lag on private contracts); government contracts use quarterly WPI-based escalation. Switchgear delivery lead times have stretched from 4-6 weeks to 3-4 months due to the war.

Payments: central government payments not an issue, except a Central University project in Himachal unpaid for 5 months. Assam receipts resumed after elections, with major chunks received in the last 15 days.
